drivers.title: Iran strikes more tankers in Hormuz; oil rebounds toward $100
drivers.rationale: Mines and strikes keep physical Hormuz flows impaired while odds of the blockade ending by 15 November are only 8% -> after a 14% five-day drop, crude has room to rebound -> producers gain short term, airlines lag. Political pressure to end the war caps the upside.

drivers.title: Oil plunges as Trump says an Iran deal 'could happen'; Iran offers a 48-hour Hormuz reopening for sanctions relief
drivers.rationale: A deal that reopens Hormuz would remove most of the remaining war premium (Brent is still +4% in 20 days) -> producers lag, airlines gain. Monday's 11% drop already priced a lot, and the overnight US strikes show the talks can still fail, so confidence is low.

drivers.title: Tankers hit mines and a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz; ceasefire odds fall
drivers.rationale: Attacks on shipping plus falling ceasefire odds and talk of a post-midterm campaign -> energy majors gain, airlines lose. Brent is already +12% in 20 days, so the size is moderate. This cuts against yesterday's low-confidence call that diplomacy would ease the oil premium; the money has moved toward escalation.
